Lessons.Title: Problems with Equal Groups of Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will apply your understandings about multiplication of a fraction by a whole number to solve problems.
Key idea: Fraction multiplication models help solve equal-group contexts, including recipes and repeated measures.
How to reason: Identify the amount per serving and number of servings, multiply exactly, then name the correct unit.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up: True or False: Two and Three Factors (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1: Banana Bread Recipe (15 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as A bakery is making banana bread. Here is the recipe for 1 batch., 1 banana, \(\frac{2}{3}\), \(\frac{3}{2}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2: How Much Milk Was Used? (20 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{1}{10}\), On Monday, the bakery sold 8 servings of milkshake. How much milk was used?, On Tuesday, two customers bought 4 servings of milkshake each. How much milk was used?, On Wednesday, four customers bought 2 servings of milkshake each. How much milk was used?. First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
Original source Cool-down is access-restricted/unverified; Edulytics substitutes goal-aligned independently authored teacher-reviewed exit prompt.
Edulytics worked model: Each serving uses 1/10 litre of milk. Eight servings use how much?. Explain every transformation and check using equal wholes/units.
Open reflection: The source banana bread recipe and milkshake matching activity retain teacher-reviewed context.
